title: Live startup token persisted verbatim to logs/desktop-child.log (no scrub)
repro:
# one-time setup, from the repo root
cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/Cargo.toml --bin supervisor --bin fixture-sidecar
SUP=$PWD/apps/desktop/target/debug/supervisor
FIX=$PWD/apps/desktop/target/debug/fixture-sidecar
APP=$PWD/apps/desktop/target/release/bundle/macos/arXMCP.app/Contents/MacOS/supervisor
R=/tmp/chaos-sup && rm -rf $R && mkdir -p $R
# helper: write a launch plan for $R
plan() { python3 -c "import json,sys;json.dump(dict(child_argv=[sys.argv[1]],component='arxmcp-fixture-sidecar',data_root=sys.argv[2],identity_file=sys.argv[1],smoke=sys.argv[3]=='1',version='0.1.0',**json.loads(sys.argv[4])),open(sys.argv[2]+'/launch-plan.json','w'))" "$1" "$2" "$3" "${4:-{\}}"; }
run() { env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH USER=$USER ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN=$1/launch-plan.json ${2:-$SUP}; }
FAST='{"test_bound_timeout_ms":3000,"test_shutdown_grace_ms":500,"test_shutdown_force_after_ms":500}'

cat > $R/h_echo <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
exec /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sys,time
line=sys.stdin.buffer.readline()
sys.stderr.buffer.write(b"STDERR-ECHO:"+line); sys.stderr.buffer.flush()
time.sleep(300)'
SH
chmod +x $R/h_echo
plan $R/h_echo $R 1 "$FAST"
run $R
grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' $R/logs/desktop-child.log     # <-- the LIVE startup token, on disk
pkill -f 'time.sleep(300)'
observed:
<data_root>/logs/desktop-child.log contains, unmodified:
STDERR-ECHO:{"contract":{"major":1,"minor":0},...,"shutdown":{...},"startup_token":"redacted-startup-token-a-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"}
grep -oE "[0-9a-f]{64}" returns redacted-startup-token-a-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx (the live capability for that run) plus c76ee189... (the identity digest). File mode 0644.
expected: apps/desktop/README.md "Secret handling" states the token "is never an argument, environment variable, URL/query value, `bound` field, object representation, exception detail, stdout/stderr diagnostic, or persisted manifest/log artifact." That claim is unconditional and false. lifecycle.rs wires the child stderr fd straight to a file (`stderr(Stdio::from(log_file))`) with no scrubber in the path at all. redact.rs's own module doc concedes the sink is "defended independently by the Python RedactionFilter" -- i.e. undefended against any child that is not the cooperating Python one, and undefended against the real child's NON-logging stderr writes too (CHAOS-SUP-14 shows the frozen child emitting a raw "Fatal Python error:" block straight to fd 2, bypassing logging entirely).

observed:
{"elapsed_ms":756,"event":"bound-frame-invalid","fields":{"frame_prefix":"{TOKEN=[REDACTED]} and again [REDACTED] and UPPER REDACTED-STARTUP-TOKEN-C-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and partial redacted-startup-token-c-xxxxxxx\n"},"pid":40334,"seq":3}
The exact-case occurrences became [REDACTED]; the UPPERCASE copy of the same 64-hex token and a 32-char prefix were persisted verbatim to <data_root>/logs/supervisor-events.ndjson. `tr A-F a-f` recovers the live capability.

cat > $R/evil <<'SH'

sleep 2
SH
chmod +x $R/evil
plan $R/evil $R 1 '{"test_bound_timeout_ms":1500,"test_shutdown_grace_ms":200,"test_shutdown_force_after_ms":200}'

observed:
Supervisor exits 1 (the fake child never emits `bound`) but the payload has already run:
pwned.txt: "ARBITRARY CODE RAN AS chris.dare argv0=/.../t22-releaseplan/evil"
events: child-spawn {"child_pid":65137} -> lifecycle-failed {"reason":"bound frame timeout"} -> orphan-shutdown.
codesign -dv on the same binary: Identifier=com.arxmcp.desktop, Format=app bundle with Mach-O thin (arm64), Signature=adhoc, flags=0x2(adhoc).
The other test-only knobs (test_fault, test_hide_window, test_shutdown_grace_ms, test_shutdown_force_after_ms, test_bound_timeout_ms) are honoured by the release binary too, subject only to validate_plan's smoke-mode gate.
expected: apps/desktop/README.md presents payload resolution -- child_payload_candidates -> resolve_inside (canonicalize + component-wise containment, symlinked-root refusal) -> identity_file digest check -- as the trust boundary for what the supervisor will execute. load_plan short-circuits every bit of it when ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN is set, and validate_plan checks only that child_argv is non-empty and that test knobs stay inside smoke mode; it never checks that child_argv[0] is contained anywhere, nor that identity_file names the same tree. main.rs's own header comment calls this arm "a test seam" -- but it is compiled into the release artifact. Under e4 Developer-ID signing plus hardened runtime this becomes a code-injection and TCC-inheritance vector: the attacker binary runs as the child of a signed com.arxmcp.desktop and inherits what the app was granted. Expected: gate the env arm behind cfg(debug_assertions) or a non-default feature, or subject child_argv[0] to the same containment as the self-authored arm.

R=/tmp/chaos-sup && rm -rf $R && mkdir -p $R
# helper: write a launch plan for $R

run() { env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH USER=$USER ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN=$1/launch-plan.json ${2:-$SUP}; }
FAST='{"test_bound_timeout_ms":3000,"test_shutdown_grace_ms":500,"test_shutdown_force_after_ms":500}'

RA=$R/a; RB=$R/b; mkdir -p $RA $RB
plan $FIX $RA 1 '{"test_fault":"never-ready"}'     # A holds a live child
plan $FIX $RB 1
run $RA & sleep 10
run $RB ; echo "B exit=$?"
cat $RB/logs/supervisor-events.ndjson    # ONE line, owns_lock true, no child-spawn
cat $RA/logs/supervisor-events.ndjson    # A recorded duplicate-activation
kill %1
expected: The single-instance defence is split across two scopes that do not agree. acquire_supervisor_lock is PER-DATA-ROOT (<data_root>/supervisor.lock via fs2); tauri-plugin-single-instance is MACHINE-GLOBAL (/tmp/com_arxmcp_desktop_si.sock, derived from the tauri.conf.json identifier). main.rs reasons at length about the fs2 LOSER not registering the plugin listener ("letting a lock loser register it first would kill the lock winner mid-boot"), but nothing covers two fs2 WINNERS on different roots -- both register, and the second is exited by the plugin. Expected either data-root-scoped plugin arbitration so isolated instances coexist, or -- at minimum -- an event plus a nonzero exit plus a stderr line. Exit 0 with "owns_lock: true" as the final record is an actively wrong report: a harness or CI gate reading the exit code sees success from a run that spawned nothing. This also makes any two concurrent desktop gate runs on one machine silently non-independent.
